notes.meaning: A man possessed by an evil spirit cries out while Jesus is teaching in the synagogue. The evil spirit has completely taken control of the poor man's speech and body. The devil is called an unclean spirit because he is pure evil and pollutes human lives.

The demon screams in terror, asking Jesus what business He has with them and if He has come to destroy them. Even while the religious leaders fail to see who Jesus is, the demon knows He is the Holy One of God. Evil spirits understand that the Lord has come to tear down their kingdom.
Jesus firmly orders the evil spirit to be quiet and come out of the man. He refuses to accept testimony about who He is from a demon. The Lord silences the spirit by His own divine power and command.

The unclean spirit throws the man into a violent fit and screams out as it leaves. Even though the demon tries to hurt the man on its way out, it is forced to obey Christ. Jesus rescues the helpless man from the grip of Satan.

Everyone in the synagogue is shocked and begins talking about what just took place. They recognize that Jesus brings fresh teaching backed by real divine authority, commanding even foul spirits with full obedience. His miracles prove that His message comes straight from God.

News about what Jesus did travels fast through the entire region of Galilee. People carry the report from one neighbor to another by word of mouth. This public miracle makes Jesus well known all across the countryside.

After leaving the synagogue service, Jesus walks with James and John straight to the home of Simon Peter and Andrew. The disciples welcome the Lord into their private family home. Jesus cares about our daily home life just as much as our gatherings for worship.

Simon Peter's mother-in-law is lying in bed with a dangerous, burning fever. The disciples tell Jesus about her condition as soon as He arrives. We should bring our sick family members to the Lord in prayer.

differ.view: Many evangelicals teach that Peter was clearly married because he had a mother-in-law, showing that Christian leaders are free to marry.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching holds that priestly celibacy is a discipline of the church rather than an unchangeable doctrine, and some suggest Peter may have been a widower by this time.

notes.meaning: Jesus goes to her bedside, takes her by the hand, and helps her stand up. The fever leaves her body instantly, and she begins serving a meal to her guests. When the Lord restores our health, we should gladly use our strength to serve Him and others.

When the sun sets and the Sabbath day of rest comes to an end, the townspeople carry all their sick and demon-possessed friends to Jesus. They wait until evening so they will not break Jewish Sabbath laws against carrying loads. People come running to Christ because they know He has the power to relieve their suffering.

A huge crowd from all over the town crowds around the front door of Simon Peter's home. People gather to bring their loved ones for help and to see the wondrous works of Jesus. Great crowds are drawn to the Lord when they hear of His goodness.

Jesus heals many people who suffer from all sorts of illnesses and casts out many demons. He does not allow the demons to speak because they know He is the Messiah. Jesus refuses to let evil spirits be the witnesses who announce His holy identity.

Very early the next morning, while it is still dark outside, Jesus gets up and slips away to an empty place to pray. Even after working late into the night healing crowds, He makes quiet time with His Father His top priority. Time spent alone in prayer gives us strength for our daily duties.

Simon Peter and the other disciples realize Jesus is missing and search eagerly for Him. They hunt through the hills until they track Him down in His quiet place of prayer. The disciples are anxious for Jesus to return to the growing crowds in town.

When the disciples finally find Jesus, they tell Him that everyone is searching for Him. They want Him to come back to Capernaum right away to meet the enthusiastic crowd. The disciples think popular success should keep Jesus in one place.

Jesus answers that they must travel on to the nearby village towns instead. He explains that His true purpose is to preach the good news in other places as well. Preaching God's message of salvation is the main reason Jesus came into the world.

Jesus travels throughout the whole province of Galilee, preaching in the Jewish synagogues and casting out evil spirits. He travels from town to town sharing the word of the kingdom of God. His powerful deeds prove that His message is completely true.

A man with leprosy falls on his knees before Jesus and begs to be made clean. Leprosy was a painful skin disease that forced victims to live away from society and worship. The man shows strong faith by believing Jesus has full power to heal him if He chooses to do so.

differ.view: Many Charismatic Christians teach that God always desires to heal physical sickness in this life if believers pray with full faith.
Many evangelicals teach that while God can heal any disease, He does not promise to heal all physical illness in this present life.

notes.meaning: Filled with deep mercy, Jesus reaches out His hand and touches the diseased man, saying that He is willing to make him clean. Under Jewish law, touching a leper made a person ceremonially unclean, but Jesus brings pure cleansing instead. His loving touch brings comfort to an outcast who had been avoided by others for years.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: A few early Greek manuscripts read that Jesus was indignant or angry rather than moved with compassion, which scholars suggest was anger against the destructive power of disease.

notes.meaning: The moment Jesus finishes speaking, the disease leaves the man's body completely. He is cured immediately, and his skin becomes entirely healthy and whole. The mighty word of Christ has the power to undo disease in a single instant.

Jesus immediately sends the healed man on his way with a stern warning. He speaks firmly to make sure the man follows His exact instructions without delay. Jesus wants obedience before anything else takes place.

Jesus tells the man not to talk to anyone on the road, but to go straight to the priest and offer the sacrifices required by the Law of Moses. Only a priest had the legal right to pronounce a leper clean so he could return to his family and town. This official inspection serves as public proof that God has healed him.

Instead of following orders, the man goes out and tells everyone about his miraculous healing. Because the crowds become so overwhelming, Jesus can no longer walk openly into the towns and must stay out in deserted areas. Even out in the wilderness, people from every direction still come to find Him.
